headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from untrusted workflow outputs into a prompt-leakage target; other risks are limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: argo-workflows can emit artifacts and parameters over REST/gRPC, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage. No shared channel is documented, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low. The pathway is plausible if Argo outputs are consumed as instructions by the other agent.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-produced artifacts or parameters as instructions
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace, queue, or copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Add a strict content-type boundary between workflow outputs and prompts
Require provenance tags on all agent-to-agent messages
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from artifacts
Review any shared filesystem or queue wiring
requires-engineering: add sandboxed parsing and allowlists for inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while agent_b has no documented data classes or egress. No shared workspace or sensitive class is documented, so leakage is possible only through an external bridge or operator handling, making the blast radius limited and the pathway unusual.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts contain sensitive parameters and are copied into agent_b inputs
IF an operator exports agent_b outputs into a third-party service
mitigations: Keep sensitive parameters out of shared artifacts
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Redact secrets before handoff
Turn off any automatic export of outputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: argo-workflows has REST/gRPC API access and can manage workflow state, but system_prompts_leaks shows no write surfaces or concurrency model. Because overlapping mutable-resource writes are not documented, a direct conflict is not established; uncertainty remains, but the pair does not show a default shared-write hazard.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external resource
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable directory or API token
mitigations: Separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared writable directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Audit API scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts/parameters that another system may treat as inputs, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage-oriented target that may surface or reuse text. The pairwise cascade is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low because default handoffs can propagate unverified content into downstream behavior.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without verification
IF agent_a-generated text is rendered or acted on downstream
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default
Limit downstream actions to read-only review
Log and diff handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent payloads

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling mismatch is documented for either agent. argo-workflows is open-source with docs-only evidence, and system_prompts_leaks has no compliance surface described, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployment places regulated data into either agent
IF a jurisdiction-specific retention policy is introduced
mitigations: Document data residency for each deployment
Classify data before routing it to either agent
Add retention settings to the workflow policy
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing
